scenarios.title: DELETE removes existing book and returns 204
scenarios.given: Book store has a book with id 1 in memory.
scenarios.then: Response is 204 with no body and GET /books/1 then returns 404.

scenarios.title: DELETE returns 404 for nonexistent book
scenarios.given: Book store has books but not id 999.

logic: BookStore must expose a thread-safe delete(id) method that removes the book with the integer id from the in-memory store; it returns the removed book (or None) and ensures ids never reused after deletion.

DELETE request handler must first validate the path id is an integer (exactly one digit sequence; reject non-integer strings like 'abc' via ValueError catch on int() conversion) and return 400 with JSON {'error': '<message>'} if invalid.
DELETE handler must look up the book by id in the BookStore; if not found, return 404 with JSON {'error': '<message>'} (covers S10 nonexistent book case).
Once a valid, existing book id is found, the handler calls BookStore.delete(id) to remove it and then sends a 204 response with no body and no content (no JSON body, Content-Length 0).
No disk writes occur; all deletion state is in-memory only.
The handler must not accept any body on DELETE; any malformed body is still handled by the generic 400 error path.
